coverage_notes.US: Primary source is ETF Central's weekly 'ETF News You Missed This Week' recaps for the weeks of Jul 6 through Oct 16, 2026 (15 weeks). These recaps give the launch week but almost never an exact first-trading date, so launch_date is null for every row except Corgi's eight bond/money-market ETFs (Oct 16, 2026) and HAWG (Aug 14, 2026); the week is recoverable from source_url. Exchange is null unless the recap named it. GAPS: (1) Oct 19-23, 2026 is not covered: the ETF Central recap for that week was not yet published (404) and wire-service searches returned nothing in-window. (2) Jul 1-3, 2026 is not covered: the Jun 29-Jul 3 recap (fetched) lists ~28 launches (Corgi July-series buffers, PGIM quarterly buffers, AllianzIM JULI, ARK ARKE, Kurv KMEM, Tema DISK/LAZR, First Eagle FESC/FECM, Defiance RANK, Tradr 2x funds, Skylar MWHS) but gives no dates, so they could not be confirmed as on/after Jul 1 and were excluded. (3) etf.com launch tracker and mutualfunds.com returned HTTP 403; no issuer press releases or exchange listing pages were fetched, so no row is cross-verified against a second source. Rows rest on the WebFetch summarizer's reading of each recap. EXCLUDED: ETNs (BMO/REX MicroSectors), products without a stated ticker or name (Corgi's unnamed 2x single-stock batches in July, a YieldMax memory income fund, Grayscale spot Zcash product, Mast HXA/HXE/HXC, Tradr METQ/AXTQ/COHQ/LWLX), Corgi buffer tickers listed without names (AUGC, CAUG, CTAU, HAUG, QAU, QQAU, IDAU, EMAU, SCAU, week of Aug 3-7), Morgan Stanley Ethereum/Solana Trusts (MSSE/MSOL; structure not stated), Alaia MPDB (ticker conflict with link MPDP), SoFi SFYI (ticker conflict with link SYFI), Guinness Atkinson GAIQ (fund name not given), and the JPMorgan GARP conversion (no ticker). FactSet (search result) reported 106 new US ETFs in September 2026 alone, so this dataset is a broad sample, not a complete census; the recaps themselves may omit launches. CAVEATS: some rows are mutual-fund conversions or ETF share classes of existing funds (BAGX, BRSV, BUSM, RJCA, ZINN, ZDIS, CTAG, TIZE, FFLX from closed-end FCT, HWIV, HWO, HWGV, HWMV, DLCU, DFGV, SECA via Section 351). Direxion's six Defined Income Boost tickers are not mapped to individual names in the source. Issuers are normalized to brand: T-REX funds -> 'REX Shares' (co-sponsored with Tuttle), T-Strive and Tuttle-Rareview -> 'Tuttle Capital Management', Exchange Traded Concepts white-label funds -> the named partner brand (xETFs, Kiwoom Securities, ARIAM Global, Viking Fund Management), FT Vest -> 'First Trust', Leverage Shares by Themes -> 'Leverage Shares'. Category is assigned by name/description and is a judgment call.
coverage_notes.Canada: launch_date is the first trading day only where a fetched release or recap stated it ("begins trading today" or an explicit date). Otherwise it is null and the row is placed in the window by a monthly or weekly roundup (Globe and Mail, Cboe Canada weekly recap, Investment Executive, ETF Express). Null-date rows: NSDC (advisor.ca says 'as of July 9'), ZCDX/ZCDX.U (BMO release of July 30 says 'listed and trading'; a TSX bulletin snippet says July 29), PBY (Globe lists it under July, Cboe under Aug 24-28), TBCK, ZABS x3 (release Aug 27 says 'listed and trading'; a third-party page cites Aug 17), ROSY/TPUT (announced Sept 9; ROSY offering closed Sept 8), TQID (TD release Sept 17, but ETF Facts start date is July 23, both in the window), Manulife x4 (announced Sept 29), NBI x5 (September), Middlefield x2, HONE (week of Sept 28-Oct 2). Date conflicts resolved toward the issuer release: HPYG (Harvest release July 7; advisor.ca says July 8); Global X PowerStock (release Oct 14; Cboe page shows TSLP launched 10/13); PAYT (Brompton release Oct 19; a search snippet claimed 10/15). NAGF and CI Forge (CCAF, CCAF.U, CLSF) rest only on the Cboe Canada ETF news page's 'Newly launched funds' list; no issuer release was found, and the exchange is not stated. Exchange is null where the supporting page does not name it; the Globe '-T' ticker suffix was not treated as evidence. Issuer: iShares-branded and RBC-branded funds are both recorded as 'RBC iShares' (alliance branding used in the releases); split them by fund name if needed. Hamilton/Westcourt WHYP is recorded under Hamilton ETFs (issuing release). Avantis CIBC funds are under CIBC Asset Management. Excluded: launches before July 1 (Desjardins DACU/DACL/DAGL June 29; NBI NCNS/NBLD/NGRW/NEQT/NTHM June 23; Purpose SPXY June 15); Caldwell CPIF/UDA (Canadian Securities Exchange, not TSX/Cboe); new unit classes of existing ETFs (Brompton SPLT.U, Evolve HISA.L/HISU.V); Guardian GICD/GIGD (Kalkine calls them 'newly launched' at an August bell ceremony, but they are absent from July/August roundups and no first-trading date was found); Brompton PAYB (named only in a search summary, never on a fetched page); Harvest IonQ fund (in the prospectus only, no launch found); the AGGX-NE/RBC row in the Globe September extract (looks like a parsing error; RNWH is recorded instead). Not covered: the TMX new-listings bulletins (tsx.com reported 'websites are currently unavailable'); Cboe weekly recaps for July 13-17 (HTTP 500) and October 12-16 / 19-23 (404 or not yet published), so launches from Oct 16-23 other than PAYT and NEI may be missing; no October monthly roundup existed yet. Morningstar Canada, Canadian Investment Review and Wealth Professional were not systematically checked. Some fields came from search-result summaries (e.g. GIAI July 28, TECY Aug 13, CAMO Aug 20, VCOR Sept 9, ZACU Sept 24, CMIG Sept 15, FGQE Oct 1, Ninepoint Sept 14, WHYP Sept 10) rather than full-page fetches. One fetch summary (TradingView NEI) returned wrong tickers; the newswire.ca original was used instead, so treat other summary-only fields with similar caution. Category is my own classification from the fund name and description, not a source field. BlossomCon: the sponsor list comes from the official tour page, which gives only a general list plus Toronto tour sponsors; no Vancouver- or NYC-specific sponsors are listed. A search summary also called Harvest the presenting sponsor for the 3rd straight year and mentioned 14 sponsor activations, but I did not verify this on a fetched page. No 2027 dates were found beyond the NYC 'Rescheduled to April' note.
